newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras discovers two more common graves.
newsitem.headline: Honduras discovers two more common graves.

text.p: Clandestine graves filled with human remains have been unearthed on the grounds of an army barracks and at a ranch of a retired army colonel, officials in Honduras said on Sunday.
News of the two discoveries came just days after five other burial sites were found filled with the bones of presumed leftists who fell victim to military repression in the 1980s.
"The earth of Honduras is mined with clandestine cemeteries," said Berthe Oliva, coordinator of Honduras' Committee of the Families of Disappeared Prisoners.
She said she believed the newly discovered common graves also contained the remains of missing leftists.
It was not clear how many bodies each grave contained.

Leo Valladares, head of the Honduras government's Human Rights Commission, announced the discovery on Sunday. He said that investigations had to be carried out to establish the identity of the bodies and he would ask judicial authorities to push ahead with the excavations.
The discoveries were made on the grounds of a unit of Honduras's Special Forces to the east of the capital and on a ranch in the north owned by retired army colonel Amilcar Zelaya, Valladares said.
He did not say how the discoveries were made.
Death squads made up of police and military personnel "disappeared" at least 184 people and murdered dozens more during Honduras' dirty war in the 1980s.
Most of the killings took place between 1982 and 1984, when the Honduran military was led by Gen. Gustavo Alvarez, an ardent anti-communist gunned down by leftists in 1990.
The U.S. Central Intelligence Agency and the Argentine military trained Honduras' secret services at the time, and Valladares has said he wants to clear up what role each played in the killings.
A month ago Washington promised to release previously classified information about the CIA's "anti-insurgency" role in the Central American country, but so far Argentina has been less forthcoming.
